indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.5.2.1: Know common diseases of humans, causes, symptoms, effects and prevention
indicator.objective: Know how common skin diseases can be prevented

skills.description: Identify ways to prevent skin diseases
Demonstrate or role-play a prevention scenario

misconceptions: You only need to bathe when you are dirty.
Sharing towels is fine as long as you are friends.
Skin diseases go away on their own without treatment.

questions.stem: How can you prevent skin diseases?
options: Bathe regularly with soap and water
questions.explanation: Bathing regularly with soap and water removes dirt and germs, helping prevent skin diseases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not link bathing to disease prevention.

questions.stem: Why should you not share your towel with a friend?
options: The towel might be too small
questions.explanation: Sharing a towel can spread germs that cause skin diseases like ringworm.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sharing is always safe.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common skin disease?
hints: It causes a round, itchy patch.
questions.explanation: Ringworm is a common skin disease caused by a fungus.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse skin diseases with other illnesses.

questions.stem: Why is it important to prevent skin diseases?
hints: Skin diseases can be itchy and painful.
questions.explanation: Preventing skin diseases keeps you healthy and avoids discomfort.

questions.stem: What should you do after playing in the sand to prevent skin problems?
options: Wipe your hands on your clothes
questions.explanation: Washing your hands and bathing after playing in the sand removes dirt and prevents skin irritation.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not clean up after play.

questions.stem: Ama has ringworm. What should she do to prevent spreading it to her sister?
options: Not share her towel or clothes and wash them separately
questions.explanation: Not sharing personal items and washing them separately prevents the fungus from spreading.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize how contagious ringworm is.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common skin disease in children?
hints: It causes red spots on the skin.
questions.explanation: Measles is a viral disease that causes a red rash on the skin.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse measles with non-skin diseases.

questions.stem: Why is it important to keep your skin dry after bathing?
options: Fungus grows well in warm, wet places
questions.explanation: Drying your skin removes moisture, making it harder for fungi that cause skin diseases to grow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the link between wet skin and fungal infections.

questions.stem: What can you do to prevent heat rashes?
options: Wear light, clean clothes and bathe regularly
Wear heavy clothes in the sun
hints: Heat rashes happen when you sweat.
questions.explanation: Wearing light, clean clothes and bathing regularly helps prevent sweat from irritating the skin.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know what causes heat rashes.

questions.stem: If you notice a red, itchy patch on your skin, what should you do?
options: Tell a parent or teacher and go to a clinic
hints: It might be a skin disease.
questions.explanation: Telling an adult and seeking medical help ensures proper treatment and prevents spreading.

questions.stem: Name one way to prevent skin diseases.
hints: What do you do in the bathroom?
questions.explanation: Bathing regularly and not sharing personal items are ways to prevent skin diseases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may say 'taking medicine' (prevention is about hygiene).

questions.stem: Name one common skin disease.
questions.explanation: Ringworm, measles, and eczema are common skin diseases.

questions.stem: Why is it important to wash your clothes regularly to prevent skin diseases?
options: Dirty clothes can trap sweat and dirt, causing skin irritation or infections
hints: Sweat and dirt stay on clothes.
questions.explanation: Dirty clothes trap sweat and dirt against the skin, creating an environment where germs and fungi can grow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think clothes only need washing when visibly dirty.

questions.stem: How does keeping your finger nails short and clean help prevent skin diseases?
options: It stops dirt and germs from collecting under the nails and spreading to your skin
It makes your nails grow faster
hints: Short nails are easier to clean.
questions.explanation: Short, clean nails prevent dirt and germs from accumulating and causing skin infections.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think nail care is only cosmetic.

questions.stem: Role-play a scenario where you show a younger sibling how to bathe properly to prevent skin diseases.

criteria.description: Demonstrates correct bathing steps (wet, soap, scrub, rinse, dry)
Explains why each step is important for preventing skin diseases

questions.explanation: This tests the practical understanding of hygiene practices.

questions.stem: Act out how you would explain to a friend why they should not share their comb.

criteria.description: States that sharing combs can spread skin diseases or lice
Suggests a safer alternative (e.g., using your own comb)

hints: Think about what stays on a comb.
questions.explanation: This tests communication about preventing the spread of skin infections.

questions.stem: Write down two ways to prevent ringworm from spreading in a household.

criteria.description: States not sharing towels, clothes, or combs
States keeping the skin clean and dry

hints: What items should not be shared?
What should the skin be like?
questions.explanation: Not sharing personal items and keeping the skin dry prevent the spread of ringworm.

questions.stem: Explain why good personal hygiene is the best way to prevent skin diseases.

criteria.description: States that hygiene removes germs and dirt
States that it stops the conditions that allow skin diseases to spread

questions.explanation: Good hygiene removes the dirt and germs that cause skin diseases and prevents them from spreading.

questions.stem: A family shares one bar of soap for bathing. One child has a skin infection. What is the BEST advice?
options: Use separate soaps or liquid soap to prevent spreading the infection
Use the soap only on the infected child
hints: Soap can carry germs from one person to another.
questions.explanation: Using separate soaps prevents the infection from spreading via the shared bar of soap.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not think soap can transmit germs.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher three things you do every day to keep your skin healthy and prevent diseases.

criteria.description: Names a second action (e.g., wearing clean clothes)
Names a third action (e.g., not sharing personal items)

hints: What do you do in the morning?
What do you do after playing?
questions.explanation: Daily habits like bathing, wearing clean clothes, and not sharing personal items keep the skin healthy.
